work.title: Jack Sprat
work.note: Jack Sprat é uma cantiga tradicional inglesa conhecida desde o século XVII. Os versos falam de um casal de gostos opostos: Jack não come gordura e a mulher não come carne magra, e assim os dois, juntos, deixam o prato limpo. pages.title: No cashier today · 1/3
paragraphs: Tom lives in **Houston**. His fridge is empty. There is no cheese, no bread and no fruit, so it is time to **stock up**. He goes to the supermarket with a cart.

At the end of the store, there are no cashiers. Tom goes to the self-checkout. “**Excuse me, how does this work?**” he asks. Rosa works at the store. “**Scan each item, then pay.**” “**Where do I scan?**” “**Here, on the red light.**”
pages.prompt: Onde começa e o que acontece?

pages.title: No cashier today · 2/3
paragraphs: Tom scans the cheese and the bread. Then the machine says, “unexpected item.” “**Put it in the bag first**,” Rosa says. Tom puts the bread in the bag. “**Oh, I see. Now it works.**”
“**How do I weigh the apples?**” Tom asks. “**Choose ‘produce’ on the screen.**” Tom touches the screen and puts the apples and three lemons on the scale. The bag is heavy now.

pages.title: No cashier today · 3/3
paragraphs: At home, Tom thinks about “Jack Sprat,” an old English rhyme. Jack could eat no fat, and his wife could eat no lean, so between the two of them they cleaned the platter. Tom smiles. Now his fridge is full, and he does not **run out of** food.
